6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicEtCoverBridge
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.OverSigmaExtension
8	import Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Sites.Representability
9	
10	/-!
11	# The big-site Zariski sheaf `pic⁰` and the 01JJ seam (DAT-6, stage 3)
12	
13	The slice trick assembled: the Σ-extension of the degree-zero Picard functor is an
14	honest sheaf for the big Zariski topology on `Scheme`, and mathlib's 01JJ
15	local-representability engine applied to it descends to a representation of the
16	degree-zero Picard functor itself on the slice.
17	
18	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0TypeFunctor C`: the degree-zero Picard functor with values in
19	  types — the `forget₂ ⋙ forget` massage of `pic0Functor`, owned here once
20	  (`pic0TypeFunctor_obj`/`pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply` are `rfl`).
21	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0SigmaFunctor C : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u`: the Σ-extension
22	  `T ↦ Σ (a : T ⟶ Spec k), pic⁰(Over.mk a)` — the big-site carrier.
23	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf` / **`pic0SigmaSheaf C`**: the sheaf
24	  certificate.  By mathlib's own reduction the big-site sheaf condition collapses to
25	  elementwise ∃!-amalgamation on honest open covers
26	  (`Precoverage.isSheaf_toGrothendieck_iff_of_isStableUnderBaseChange`,
27	  `exists_cover_of_mem_pretopology`, `Presieve.isSheafFor_arrows_iff` — the
28	  `BigZariski` TODO is never touched): the Σ-components glue by
29	  `Scheme.Cover.glueMorphisms`, the fibre components glue by the DAT-6 stage-1
30	  evaluation bridge (`pic0Subgroup_existsUnique_of_cover`), and the two layers are
31	  stitched by the stage-2 amalgamation seam (`sigmaExtension_map_mk_eq_iff`) and
32	  compatibility descent (`map_eq_of_sigmaExtension_map_eq`).
33	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`: **the DAT-glue seam** — given a
34	  chart family of relatively representable open immersions into `pic0SigmaSheaf`
35	  (DAT-C) that is jointly locally surjective (DAT-B), mathlib's
36	  `Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy` produces a representation of the
37	  Σ-extension by the glued scheme, and the stage-2 Σ-descent `overSlice` turns it
38	  into a representation of `pic0TypeFunctor C` by the glued scheme over the
39	  Σ-component of the universal element.
40	-/
41	
42	set_option autoImplicit false
43	
44	universe u
45	
46	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite
47	
48	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
49	
50	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
51	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
52	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
53	
54	/-! ## The type-valued degree-zero Picard functor -/
55	
56	/-- The degree-zero Picard functor with values in types: the `forget₂ ⋙ forget`
57	massage of `pic0Functor`, owned here once for the Σ-extension statements. -/
58	noncomputable abbrev pic0TypeFunctor : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u :=
59	  (pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) ⋙ forget GrpCat
60	
61	@[simp]
62	lemma pic0TypeFunctor_obj (T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ) :
63	    (pic0TypeFunctor C).obj T = pic0Subgroup C T.unop :=
64	  rfl
65	
66	lemma pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply {T T' : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ} (g : T ⟶ T')
67	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C T.unop) :
68	    (pic0TypeFunctor C).map g lam = pic0Map C g.unop lam :=
69	  rfl
70	
71	/-! ## The Σ-extension as a presheaf on the big site -/
72	
73	/-- **The big-site carrier of the slice trick**: the Σ-extension of the type-valued
74	degree-zero Picard functor, `T ↦ Σ (a : T ⟶ Spec k), pic⁰(Over.mk a)`.  Reducible so
75	that the stage-2 `sigmaExtension` calculus applies syntactically. -/
76	noncomputable abbrev pic0SigmaFunctor : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u :=
77	  Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (pic0TypeFunctor C)
78	
79	variable [GeometricallyReduced C.hom]
80	
81	set_option maxHeartbeats 800000 in
82	-- The amalgamation seams unify the `forget₂ ⋙ forget` massage of `pic0Functor`
83	-- against the Σ-extension calculus by unfolding; within the DAT-2/PicEtMap 1600000
84	-- precedent.
85	/-- **The big-site Zariski sheaf certificate of the Σ-extension** (DAT-6 keystone,
86	worksheet §1.2 site gap 1): mathlib's reduction collapses the sheaf condition to
87	elementwise ∃!-amalgamation on honest open covers, where the Σ-components glue by
88	`Scheme.Cover.glueMorphisms` and the fibre components by the stage-1 evaluation
89	bridge. -/
90	theorem pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf :
91	    Presieve.IsSheaf Scheme.zariskiTopology (pic0SigmaFunctor C) := by
92	  rw [Precoverage.isSheaf_toGrothendieck_iff_of_isStableUnderBaseChange]
93	  intro Y S hS
94	  obtain ⟨𝓤, rfl⟩ := Scheme.exists_cover_of_mem_pretopology hS
95	  rw [Presieve.isSheafFor_arrows_iff]
96	  intro x hx
97	  -- glue the Σ-components along the scheme-level cover
98	  have hpair : ∀ i j, pullback.fst (𝓤.f i) (𝓤.f j) ≫ (x i).1
99	      = pullback.snd (𝓤.f i) (𝓤.f j) ≫ (x j).1 := fun i j =>
100	    congrArg Sigma.fst
101	      (hx i j (pullback (𝓤.f i) (𝓤.f j)) (pullback.fst _ _) (pullback.snd _ _)
102	        pullback.condition)
103	  obtain ⟨aY, ha⟩ : ∃ aY : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k), ∀ i, 𝓤.f i ≫ aY = (x i).1 :=
104	    ⟨𝓤.glueMorphisms (fun i => (x i).1) hpair,
105	      fun i => 𝓤.ι_glueMorphisms (fun i => (x i).1) hpair i⟩
106	  -- the induced slice cover of `Over.mk aY` and its member sections
107	  haveI hop : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion
108	      ((Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY)).left :=
109	    fun i => 𝓤.map_prop i
110	  have hcov : ∀ p : (Over.mk aY).left, ∃ i, p ∈ Scheme.Hom.opensRange
111	      ((Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY)).left := by
112	    intro p
113	    obtain ⟨i, y, hy⟩ := 𝓤.exists_eq p
114	    exact ⟨i, y, hy⟩
115	  -- the fibre components are a compatible family on the slice cover
116	  have hcompat : ∀ (i j : 𝓤.I₀) (Z : Over (Spec (.of k)))
117	      (gi : Z ⟶ Over.mk ((x i).1)) (gj : Z ⟶ Over.mk ((x j).1)),
118	      gi ≫ (Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY)
119	          = gj ≫ (Over.homMk (𝓤.f j) (ha j) : Over.mk ((x j).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY) →
120	      pic0Map C gi ((x i).2) = pic0Map C gj ((x j).2) := by
121	    intro i j Z gi gj hg
122	    have hleft : gi.left ≫ 𝓤.f i = gj.left ≫ 𝓤.f j := congrArg Over.Hom.left hg
123	    have hdesc := Over.map_eq_of_sigmaExtension_map_eq gi gj
124	      (hx i j Z.left gi.left gj.left hleft)
125	    rwa [pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply, pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply] at hdesc
126	  -- glue the fibre components by the stage-1 evaluation bridge
127	  obtain ⟨s, hs, hsu⟩ := pic0Subgroup_existsUnique_of_cover
128	    (fun i => (Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY))
129	    hcov (fun i => (x i).2) hcompat
130	  refine ⟨⟨aY, s⟩, fun i => ?_, ?_⟩
131	  · -- the glued Σ-element restricts to the members
132	    refine (Over.sigmaExtension_map_mk_eq_iff (𝓤.f i) (ha i) s ((x i).2)).mpr ?_
133	    rw [pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply]
134	    exact hs i
135	  · -- uniqueness: Σ-components by `hom_ext`, fibres by bridge separation
136	    rintro ⟨a', s'⟩ ht'
137	    obtain rfl : aY = a' := 𝓤.hom_ext aY a' fun i =>
138	      (ha i).trans (congrArg Sigma.fst (ht' i) : 𝓤.f i ≫ a' = (x i).1).symm
139	    refine congrArg (Sigma.mk aY) (hsu s' fun i => ?_)
140	    have hmem := (Over.sigmaExtension_map_mk_eq_iff (𝓤.f i) (ha i) s' ((x i).2)).mp
141	      (ht' i)
142	    rwa [pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply] at hmem
143	
144	/-- **The Σ-extension of the degree-zero Picard functor, bundled as a sheaf on the
145	big Zariski site** — the object mathlib's 01JJ local-representability engine
146	consumes. -/
147	noncomputable def pic0SigmaSheaf : Sheaf Scheme.zariskiTopology.{u} (Type u) :=
148	  ⟨pic0SigmaFunctor C,
149	    (isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_of_type _ _).mpr (pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf C)⟩
150	
151	/-! ## The DAT-glue seam -/
152	
153	/-- **The DAT-glue statement (worksheet §4, DAT-glue row)**: a chart family of
154	relatively representable open immersions into the Σ-extension sheaf (DAT-C's
155	certificates) that is jointly Zariski-locally surjective (DAT-B's coverage) induces —
156	through mathlib's 01JJ engine and the stage-2 Σ-descent — a representation of the
157	type-valued degree-zero Picard functor by the glued scheme placed over the
158	Σ-component of the universal element.  The represented object's `.left` is
159	`(Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued` and its `.hom` is the universal
160	element's Σ-component, both definitionally. -/
161	noncomputable def pic0RepresentableByOfCharts
162	    {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
163	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
164	    (hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (f i))
165	    [Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)] :
166	    (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy
167	      (Over.mk ((Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).homEquiv
168	        (𝟙 (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued)).1) :=
169	  (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).overSlice
170	
171	end AlgebraicGeometry

8	/-!
9	# THE ATLAS IS CHART-PARAMETER HETEROGENEOUS — each chart may carry its own `n`
10	
11	`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack.lean` establishes that at a chart index legal at parameter
12	`n` the coverage theorem's threshold is forced to equal `n`, and that at `n = g` the resulting
13	hypothesis is false.  Both that file and the review it adjudicates (I-0660) then reason about
14	"the" chart parameter, as though the atlas had one.
15	
16	**It does not, and this file proves it.**  `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`
17	(`Picard/Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:161`) takes a family `f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ pic0SigmaSheaf`
18	indexed by an arbitrary `ι`, with `X : ι → Scheme` and a *per-index* certificate
19	`hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (f i)`.  Nothing ties the `X i` together, so nothing ties
20	their chart parameters together either: `mixedParamChart` below builds such a family from a
21	per-index parameter `nn : ι → ℕ`, a per-index representation of `divFunctor C π (nn i)`, and a
22	per-index chart index legal *at that index's own parameter*.
23	
24	## Why this matters, and it changes the shape of the residue
25	
26	The `b = n` calibration is per-chart.  So the question "can coverage use DAT-0a's threshold?"
27	does not have to be answered uniformly: a point whose splitting field has threshold `b_L` can be
28	covered by *the chart whose parameter is `b_L.toNat`*, and a different point by a different
29	chart.  The I-0204 non-uniformity of `m` — no single exponent works for every fibre — is
30	therefore **not** an obstruction to the atlas; it is an argument for an atlas indexed by the
31	threshold, which is what a heterogeneous family is.
32	
33	What this does **not** do, and the honest limit of the observation:
34	
35	* it does not produce the representations.  `mixedParamChart` takes `rep i` as a hypothesis, one
36	  per parameter, and the divisor-representability lane supplies `divFunctor C π g` — a single
37	  parameter.  So the heterogeneous atlas is *admissible* but not yet *inhabited* beyond `n = g`;
38	* it does not discharge `IsChartUniv` at any index (still CERT-Σ-gated, `Pic0ChartPair.lean`);
39	* it says nothing about local surjectivity, which is DAT-B B-6 and is what would actually consume
40	  the freedom.
41	
42	So the correct statement of the residue, refining `Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack`'s: **B-5's step 3
43	is a question about which parameters `divFunctor C π n` is representable at, not about
44	reconciling one parameter with one threshold.**  If representability is available only at `n = g`
45	then the slack must go into `Z` (and its legality is open, as recorded there); if it is available
46	at every `n`, coverage can be assembled chart-by-chart against each fibre's own threshold and the
47	`b = n` forcing is harmless.  That is a sharper question than either prior reading, and it is
48	addressed to the divRep lane rather than to this one.
49	
50	## Main declarations
51	
52	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mixedParamChart` — a chart family with a per-index chart parameter.
53	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isOpenImmersion_presheaf_mixedParamChart` — its `hf` clause is exactly a
54	  per-index `IsChartUniv`, so heterogeneity costs nothing in the certificate.
55	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mixedParamRepresentableBy` — such a family is admissible input to
56	  `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`.  **This is the whole point**: the DAT-glue seam never sees a
57	  chart parameter.
58	-/

61	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

63	universe u

65	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
66	
67	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
68	
69	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
70	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom π]
71	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
72	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
73	
74	noncomputable section
75	
76	variable (C π) in
77	/-- **A chart family whose chart parameter varies with the index.**
78	
79	Each index `i` carries its own degree parameter `nn i`, its own representing object `D i` of
80	`divFunctor C π (nn i)`, its own twist exponent `m i` and chart index `Z i` — the latter legal
81	*at `nn i`*, i.e. `deg_k (Z i) = (m i)·d₁ − nn i`, which is what `chartValue_mem_pic0Subgroup`
82	requires for that index's chart value to land in `pic⁰`.
83	
84	The construction is just `restrictChart` of `abelSigmaChart` applied pointwise; the content is
85	that it *typechecks*, i.e. that the target `pic0SigmaSheaf C` is parameter-free. -/
86	def mixedParamChart {ι : Type u} (nn : ι → ℕ)
87	    (D : ι → Over (Spec (.of k)))
88	    (rep : ∀ i, (divFunctor C π (nn i)).RepresentableBy (D i))
89	    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
90	    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
91	      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (nn i : ℤ))
92	    (V : ∀ i, (D i).left.Opens) (i : ι) :
93	    yoneda.obj ((V i : Scheme.{u})) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1 :=
94	  restrictChart (abelSigmaChart C π (nn i) (rep i) (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i)) (V i)
95	
96	variable (C π) in
97	/-- **Heterogeneity costs nothing in the certificate**: the `hf` clause of a mixed-parameter
98	family is exactly a per-index `IsChartUniv`, by definition of both.
99	
100	So a lane that can discharge CHART-U(c) *at one parameter* can discharge it index-by-index at
101	different parameters, with no additional compatibility between them — there is no coherence
102	condition across indices, because `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` imposes none. -/
103	theorem isOpenImmersion_presheaf_mixedParamChart {ι : Type u} (nn : ι → ℕ)
104	    (D : ι → Over (Spec (.of k)))
105	    (rep : ∀ i, (divFunctor C π (nn i)).RepresentableBy (D i))
106	    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
107	    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
108	      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (nn i : ℤ))
109	    (V : ∀ i, (D i).left.Opens)
110	    (huniv : ∀ i, IsChartUniv C π (nn i) (rep i) (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i) (V i)) (i : ι) :
111	    IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V i) :=
112	  huniv i
113	
114	variable (C π) in
115	/-- **A mixed-parameter chart family is admissible input to the DAT-glue seam.**
116	
117	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` accepts it verbatim.  This is the statement that settles the
118	question `Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack` and I-0660 both left implicit: the representability engine
119	never sees a chart parameter, so the forced calibration `b = n` is a *per-chart* condition and
120	carries no uniformity obligation.
121	
122	Note what remains hypothetical here and is not weakened by this: `hf` (i.e. `IsChartUniv`, still
123	CERT-Σ-gated), local surjectivity (DAT-B B-6), and the *existence* of `rep i` at parameters other
124	than `g` — which is the question this observation hands to the divisor-representability lane. -/
125	def mixedParamRepresentableBy {ι : Type u} (nn : ι → ℕ)
126	    (D : ι → Over (Spec (.of k)))
127	    (rep : ∀ i, (divFunctor C π (nn i)).RepresentableBy (D i))
128	    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
129	    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
130	      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (nn i : ℤ))
131	    (V : ∀ i, (D i).left.Opens)
132	    (hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V i))
133	    [Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology
134	      (Sigma.desc (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V))] :
135	    (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy
136	      (Over.mk ((Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).homEquiv
137	        (𝟙 (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued)).1) :=
138	  pic0RepresentableByOfCharts C (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V) hf
139	
140	end
141

================== I-0920 issue open
`IsPlusHonest` (the dat-b/chart-u residue) IS THE ETALE-SHEAFIFICATION GAP ASSERTED OF AN ARBITRARY SECTION -- not an open lemma. Do not send a lane at it as stated.

review-ajcr (run 0082), against chart-u's own sentence: "THE GENUINELY OPEN QUESTION ... does IsPlusHonest hold for the class a COVERAGE witness produces? A lane picking this row up should target that."

STATEMENT (Pic0ChartPlusFibreProducer.lean:200, read not paraphrased): for every affine open U of T.left, mu|U lies in the RANGE of relPicToPicEt over Gamma(T.left,U) -- Zariski-locally the class comes from the UN-sheafified relPic.

WHY STRUCTURAL. picEt rests on PicEtAff (PicEt.lean:9-21); PicEtAff C A (:218) is a QUOTIENT OVER ALL ETALE COVERS (elements PicEtAff.mk E x). PicEtAff.unit (:377), the target of relPicToPicEt (PicEtUnit.lean:126), is mk at the TRIVIAL cover `.self A` alone. So honesty says no nontrivial etale cover is needed on that piece -- exactly what the one-step plus construction exists to permit to fail.

THE PROJECT SAYS SO WHERE IT MEASURED IT: Pic0ChartHonest.lean's own "does not give" -- honesty holds "OVER Spec E.Carrier, NOT over Spec A", bought by CHANGING THE BASE, and "Nothing here performs that descent".

DISCHARGED CASES: `IsPlusHonest C T` occurs as a CONCLUSION at exactly seven sites -- either a SPECIFIC constructed class (thetaFamily/sigmaFamily/abelDiv_isPlusHonest, :245/:256/:275, each verified present) or a closure property (.mul/.inv/.pow/chartTwist). NONE concludes it for an arbitrary element of picEt.

WHY ONLY COVERAGE BITES. Chart-side uses are fine: the chart value IS abelDiv*Sigma*(theta^m)^-1, so those cases cover it -- which is why the row could be re-priced downward at all. But chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise (Pic0ChartCoveragePointwise.lean:128) quantifies over EVERY s and must hit it; arbitrariness is coverage's content, and a chart-value-shaped s is circular.

COSTING. Honesty of coverage's own WITNESS is cheap. Honesty of the class s it must HIT is the gap: the repair refines to the etale carrier and descends -- a Zariski-to-etale change of site, which pic0RepresentableByOfCharts' Zariski-locality antecedent does not absorb. Antecedent 2 owes a DECISION about which site coverage is local for, not a lemma.

NOT A REFUTATION: proving it false needs a class not Zariski-locally in relPic's image, and this tree has no Brauer machinery. The weaker sufficient claim: it is not a lemma about the tree's own constructions, and a lane told to "target that" will not find a proof.

16	unrestricted certificate, which the project's headers assert to be false**, and this file is
17	the repair.
18	
19	## The defect, measured
20	
21	`IsChartLocusFibre` (`Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean:166`) asks for a
22	`ChartFibrePresented C (abelSigmaChart …) g` at every test — the datum for the *unrestricted*
23	chart, with `W` a free structure field.  Nothing pins `W := chartLocus`, although the docstring
24	there says the `W` field "is already discharged — it is `chartLocus`".  So the open `V` never
25	enters the hypothesis, and one term gives back the unrestricted certificate:
26	
27	```
28	isOpenImmersion_presheaf_of_chartFibrePresented _ fun T g => (h T g).some
29	  : IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (abelSigmaChart …)
30	```
31	
32	That measurement is **not** repeated here: it is landed as
33	`isOpenImmersion_presheaf_abelSigmaChart_of_isChartLocusFibre` and
34	`mono_abelSigmaChart_of_isChartLocusFibre` in `Picard/Pic0ChartLocusFibreGuard.lean`, together
35	with `not_isChartLocusFibre_of_not_injective` — the criterion's own emptiness guard, finally
36	instantiated at the Abel chart.  In `isChartUniv_of_isChartLocusFibre` the restriction to `V` is
37	applied *after* the unrestricted certificate is in hand, so restricting buys nothing on the way
38	in.
39	
40	**The precise status of "false".**  `Pic0AtlasFromDivRep.lean:54`, `Pic0ChartPair.lean:14` and
41	`Pic0ChartOpenImmersionCriterion.lean:214` all assert that the Abel chart is not injective (the
42	linear system `|D|`), and by the guard above that assertion makes `IsChartLocusFibre`
43	unsatisfiable.  But **no declaration proves the non-injectivity**: the guard takes
44	`¬ Function.Injective` as a hypothesis.  So `IsChartLocusFibre` is *conditionally* unsatisfiable
45	— dead if the headers are right, and nobody has shown they are.  This file therefore does not
46	claim the old route is dead; it claims the old route is gated on a proposition the project
47	believes false and has never checked, which is reason enough not to build on it.
48	
49	The criterion itself is **not** at fault: it is stated for an arbitrary morphism of presheaves
50	and is correct.  What was wrong is the *instantiation* — at `abelSigmaChart` rather than at
51	`restrictChart (abelSigmaChart …) V`.
52	
53	## What this file provides
54	
55	* `RestrictedChartFibre` — the same datum demanded at the **restricted** chart, so
56	  `exists_factor` only has to factor test points *of `V`*.
57	* `isChartUniv_of_restrictedChartFibre` — it gives `IsChartUniv` at that same `V`, one
58	  application of the existing criterion, with no unrestricted certificate in between.
59	* `necessity_of_restrictedChartFibre` — the weakening did not delete the content: the restricted
60	  datum still forces injectivity of the restricted chart on every test.
61	* `pic0RepresentableBy_of_restrictedChartFibre` — **the `V`-coupled assembly** (inbox `I-0861`):
62	  per-index restricted fibre data on the `hf` side, and on the coverage side the containment
63	  hypothesis `hV` of `Pic0ChartAtlasCoupling.liftPointwiseToOpens`, together give the
64	  representation.  The two sides are made to share the same `V` by typing.
65	
66	## Division of labour with the two sibling files landed the same round
67	
68	`Pic0ChartLocusFibreGuard.lean` records why the *old* route must not be used, and
69	`Pic0ChartAtlasCoupling.lean` supplies the **coverage** half of the `V`-coupling
70	(`liftPointwiseToOpens`, and the converse `pointwise_of_pointwise_restrictChart` showing `hV` is
71	exactly the gap).  This file supplies the **`hf`** half — the fibre datum at the restricted
72	chart — and the assembly that consumes both.  Nothing here re-proves either sibling.
73	
74	## The honest limits, stated rather than left for a reviewer
75	
76	* **Nothing here produces any input.**  This file replaces a badly-gated route by a
77	  well-gated one; it discharges no antecedent.  `rep` (divisor representability) is a hypothesis
78	  throughout, and `IsChartUniv` is not even statable without it.
79	* **`RestrictedChartFibre` at `V = ⊥` IS inhabited — settled in
80	  `Picard/Pic0ChartRestrictedFibreSat.lean`, and an earlier draft of this section priced it
81	  wrongly.**  That draft said the `sq` field needs
82	  `Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C (Over.mk a₁))` over an empty base, "the triviality of `picEt`
83	  over the empty scheme: true, a genuinely separate lemma, and absent from the tree", and
84	  concluded that *no satisfiability witness exists at any `V`*.  **Both the pricing and the
85	  conclusion were false.**  The error was in the reduction, not the census: the `congr 1` that
86	  peeled the Σ-component and named `pic0Subgroup` threw away the fact that `pic0SigmaSheaf` is a
87	  **sheaf**, and a sheaf's value at a scheme covered by the empty sieve is terminal.  So the goal
88	  is closed by `Sheaf.isTerminalOfBotCover` applied to `Scheme.bot_mem_grothendieckTopology`
89	  (both mathlib) with no fact about `picEt` at all — `restrictedChartFibre_bot`.  The
90	  `exists_factor` half is free as `I-0861` measured; `sq` is free for a different and cheaper
91	  reason than that draft supposed.
92	* **Consequence, and it is the sharp form:** the class is non-empty, so the repaired route is not
93	  a route to an uninhabitable hypothesis, and the unmeasured-inhabitation risk that `ChartTyping`
94	  (`I-0779`) and `IsChartLocusFibre` carried does **not** apply here.  What that inhabitant also
95	  shows is that `IsChartUniv` at `V = ⊥` is free (`isChartUniv_bot`) — antecedent 1 carries no
96	  content in isolation — while the coverage clause is *refuted* at that same value
97	  (`not_coverageContainment_bot`), and at the other end `V = ⊤` the prices are swapped: coverage's
98	  containment becomes free and this datum returns the unrestricted certificate.  So the obligation
99	  is the *coupling*, and any `V` that works must be a proper intermediate open.
100	* **What that does NOT establish, since a draft of this file claimed it did** (`I-1012`): the two
101	  endpoints are **not** a non-vacuity check for the assembly below.  Two *bad* values of `V` are
102	  two refutations; non-vacuity of the pair needs a `V` where both clauses hold.  Inhabitation of
103	  the **pair** is still unmeasured at every `V`, and `necessity_of_restrictedChartFibre` is not
104	  that check either.  Only `RestrictedChartFibre` *alone* is now known inhabited.
105	* **The relation to the old form IS measured, and an earlier draft mispriced it.**  That draft
106	  said the transport `IsChartLocusFibre → RestrictedChartFibre` "needs the preimage `r ⁻¹ V`
107	  pushed forward along `W.ι`, which is real work and buys nothing".  Both halves were wrong
108	  (`I-0936`): it is `restrictedChartFibre_of_isChartLocusFibre` below, twelve lines, needing only
109	  `IsOpenImmersion.lift` — and it buys the sharp statement, because its hypothesis is exactly the
110	  coverage half's `hV`.  The "buys nothing" clause was the worse error: a lane holding the old
111	  form gets `IsChartUniv` *through the certificate three headers call false*, which is this
112	  file's whole premise.
113	-/

120	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory

122	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
123	
124	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
125	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom π] {n : ℕ}
126	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
127	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
128	
129	noncomputable section
130	
131	/-! ## The datum at the restricted chart -/
132	
133	variable (C π n) in
134	/-- **The fibre datum demanded at the restricted chart** — the repair of `IsChartLocusFibre`.
135	
136	Identical to `IsChartLocusFibre` except that the presented morphism is
137	`restrictChart (abelSigmaChart …) V` rather than `abelSigmaChart …`.  The difference is the
138	whole point: `exists_factor` now only factors test points *of `V`*, so proving it does not
139	entail that the unrestricted Abel chart is a monomorphism.
140	
141	`V` is a parameter and no choice is privileged here; the intended instantiation is the chart
142	locus, whose openness is CHART-U(b) and a separate obligation. -/
143	def RestrictedChartFibre {D : Over (Spec (.of k))}
144	    (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
145	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
146	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
147	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
148	    (V : D.left.Opens) : Prop :=
149	  ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1),
150	    Nonempty (ChartFibrePresented C
151	      (restrictChart (abelSigmaChart C π n rep m Z hdeg) V) g)
152	
153	/-- **The repaired reduction**: the restricted datum gives `IsChartUniv` at the same `V`.
154	
155	One application of the existing criterion, at the restricted chart.  Compare
156	`isChartUniv_of_isChartLocusFibre`, which applies it at the unrestricted chart and composes
157	afterwards — and therefore needs the unrestricted certificate on the way in. -/
158	theorem isChartUniv_of_restrictedChartFibre {D : Over (Spec (.of k))}
159	    (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
160	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
161	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
162	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
163	    (V : D.left.Opens) (h : RestrictedChartFibre C π n rep m Z hdeg V) :
164	    IsChartUniv C π n rep m Z hdeg V :=
165	  isOpenImmersion_presheaf_of_chartFibrePresented _ fun T g => (h T g).some
166	
167	/-- The restricted datum forces the restricted chart to be injective on every test.
168	
169	**This is NOT a non-vacuity check, and an earlier draft of this file claimed it was**
170	(`I-0937`).  Two reasons it does not carry that weight: its conclusion is *free* at `V = ⊥` with
171	no hypothesis at all (a test point of the empty open forces the test empty, hence initial); and
172	at general `V` it is `injective_of_isChartUniv` (`Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean:205`) composed with
173	`isChartUniv_of_restrictedChartFibre`, i.e. a property of *any* hypothesis implying `IsChartUniv`,
174	not evidence about this one.
175	
176	The real non-vacuity statement for the assembly is the pair `isChartUniv_bot` /
177	`not_coverageContainment_bot` in `Picard/Pic0ChartRestrictedFibreSat.lean`: `⊥` is where this
178	side is free and the coverage side is impossible, so the two hypotheses cannot both be met at a
179	convenient `V`.
180	
181	Kept because it is the right thing to cite when asking what a producer of the datum must
182	establish — the relative form of DAT-C GAP-2, over `V` rather than over `D.left`. -/
183	theorem necessity_of_restrictedChartFibre {D : Over (Spec (.of k))}
184	    (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
185	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
186	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
187	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
188	    (V : D.left.Opens) (h : RestrictedChartFibre C π n rep m Z hdeg V)
189	    (T : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ) :
190	    Function.Injective
191	      ((restrictChart (abelSigmaChart C π n rep m Z hdeg) V).app T) :=
192	  injective_of_chartFibrePresented _ (fun T' g => (h T' g).some) T
193	
194	/-! ## The transport, and what it says about the two halves of the coupling
195	
196	An earlier draft of this file priced this transport as "real work needing a pushforward" and
197	declined to prove it.  **That was wrong** (inbox `I-0936`): no preimage and no pushforward are
198	involved — keep the old datum's `W` and lift its `r` along `V.ι`. -/
199	
200	/-- **`IsChartLocusFibre` plus a range containment gives `RestrictedChartFibre`.**
201	
202	And the containment is the *same* one the coverage half owes: `hr` here is character-for-character
203	the `hV` of `Pic0ChartAtlasCoupling.liftPointwiseToOpens`, asked on the fibre side instead of the
204	coverage side.  So the two halves of the `V`-coupling are **not two obligations** — they are one
205	range containment asked twice, from opposite directions.
206	
207	This is the sharp form of "the restricted datum is weaker", and it is what makes the repair
208	precise rather than merely differently-shaped. -/
209	theorem restrictedChartFibre_of_isChartLocusFibre {D : Over (Spec (.of k))}
210	    (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
211	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
212	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
213	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
214	    (V : D.left.Opens) (h : IsChartLocusFibre C π n rep m Z hdeg)
215	    (hr : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1),
216	      Set.range (((h T g).some.r).base) ⊆ Set.range ((V.ι).base)) :
217	    RestrictedChartFibre C π n rep m Z hdeg V := by
218	  intro T g
219	  refine ⟨⟨(h T g).some.W, IsOpenImmersion.lift V.ι ((h T g).some.r) (hr T g), ?_, ?_⟩⟩
220	  · rw [restrictChart, ← Category.assoc, ← yoneda.map_comp, IsOpenImmersion.lift_fac]
221	    exact (h T g).some.sq
222	  · intro S v w hvw
223	    obtain ⟨u, hu1, hu2⟩ := (h T g).some.exists_factor S (v ≫ V.ι) w (by
224	      rw [← hvw, restrictChart]
225	      rfl)
226	    exact ⟨u, (cancel_mono V.ι).mp (by rw [Category.assoc, IsOpenImmersion.lift_fac]; exact hu1),
227	      hu2⟩
228	
229	/-! ## The `V`-coupled assembly -/
230	
231	variable (C π) in
232	/-- The `hf` clause of a mixed-parameter atlas, from per-index restricted fibre data.
233	
234	Named because the representing object of the assembly below mentions it. -/
235	theorem mixedParamHf {ι : Type u} (nn : ι → ℕ)
236	    (D : ι → Over (Spec (.of k)))
237	    (rep : ∀ i, (divFunctor C π (nn i)).RepresentableBy (D i))
238	    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
239	    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
240	      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (nn i : ℤ))
241	    (V : ∀ i, (D i).left.Opens)
242	    (huniv : ∀ i, RestrictedChartFibre C π (nn i) (rep i) (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i) (V i))
243	    (i : ι) :
244	    IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V i) :=
245	  isChartUniv_of_restrictedChartFibre (rep i) (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i) (V i) (huniv i)
246	
247	variable (C π) in
248	/-- **THE `V`-COUPLED ASSEMBLY** — the composition inbox `I-0861` names as missing.
249	
250	Antecedents 1 and 2 of `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` are *not* independent.  Coverage produces a
251	point `x : (W : Scheme) ⟶ X i` of the chart **source**, which for the real atlas is
252	`(V i : Scheme)` — so coverage has to reach the very `V i` at which `hf` was certified, and no
253	statement in the tree said so.  Here they are forced to share `V` by typing: `huniv` certifies
254	the charts at `V`, and `hcov`'s witness lands in the same `V i`.
255	
256	**This closes no gate.**  `rep`, `huniv` and `hcov` are all hypotheses and none has a producer.
257	What the statement buys is that a lane discharging `hf` and a lane discharging coverage can no
258	longer each succeed at a *different* `V` and report the pair as composed. -/
259	def pic0RepresentableBy_of_restrictedChartFibre {ι : Type u} (nn : ι → ℕ)
260	    (D : ι → Over (Spec (.of k)))
261	    (rep : ∀ i, (divFunctor C π (nn i)).RepresentableBy (D i))
262	    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
263	    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
264	      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (nn i : ℤ))
265	    (V : ∀ i, (D i).left.Opens)
266	    (huniv : ∀ i, RestrictedChartFibre C π (nn i) (rep i) (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i) (V i))
267	    [Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology
268	      (Sigma.desc (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V))] :
269	    (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy
270	      (Over.mk ((Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy
271	        (mixedParamHf C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V huniv)).homEquiv
272	        (𝟙 (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData
273	          (mixedParamHf C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V huniv)).glued)).1) :=
274	  pic0RepresentableByOfCharts C (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V)
275	    (mixedParamHf C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V huniv)
276	
277	variable (C π) in
278	/-- **The same assembly with the local-surjectivity instance produced from coverage data**, so
279	that the shared `V` is visible in the hypotheses rather than hidden in an instance binder.
280	
281	The instance version above states the seam at the named representing object (which is what the
282	`JacobianData` layer consumes); this version is the one a *coverage* lane reads, because both of
283	its geometric hypotheses mention the same `V i`: `huniv` certifies the charts there, and `hcov`'s
284	range containment — `Pic0ChartAtlasCoupling`'s `hV` — puts the coverage witness there.
285	
286	The conclusion is stated as a `Σ` only because the named object above mentions the instance this
287	definition constructs; the representing scheme is the same one. -/
288	def pic0RepresentableBy_of_restrictedChartFibre_of_coverage {ι : Type u} (nn : ι → ℕ)
289	    (D : ι → Over (Spec (.of k)))
290	    (rep : ∀ i, (divFunctor C π (nn i)).RepresentableBy (D i))
291	    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
292	    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
293	      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (nn i : ℤ))
294	    (V : ∀ i, (D i).left.Opens)
295	    (huniv : ∀ i, RestrictedChartFibre C π (nn i) (rep i) (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i) (V i))
296	    (hcov : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : ↥T),
297	      ∃ (W : T.Opens) (_ : t ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ (D i).left),
298	        (abelSigmaChart C π (nn i) (rep i) (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i)).app
299	            (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x
300	          = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s ∧
301	        Set.range (x.base) ⊆ Set.range ((V i).ι.base)) :
302	    Σ J : Over (Spec (.of k)), (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy J :=
303	  letI : Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology
304	      (Sigma.desc (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V)) :=
305	    isLocallySurjective_restrictChart_of_pointwise C
306	      (fun i => abelSigmaChart C π (nn i) (rep i) (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i)) V hcov
307	  ⟨_, pic0RepresentableBy_of_restrictedChartFibre C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V huniv⟩

  \ and :316\nisOpen_chartLocus_of_isPlusHonest.\n\nWHY IT IS NOT COSMETIC. The five\
  \ I dropped are the four PRODUCERS plus the consumer that pays\nCHART-U(b). A census\
  \ whose entire purpose was \"is there a producer of a useful shape\" enumerated\n\
  only the declarations that CANNOT be that thing, and then read their absence-of-shape\
  \ as the\nshape's absence. The conclusion survives -- I have now read all eleven\
  \ and none is a spreading-out\nor a localisation -- but it survives BY LUCK, and\
  \ a lane told \"six declarations, no producer\" might\ngo build thetaFamily_isPlusHonest,\
  \ which already exists.\n\nWHAT STANDS, unchanged and re-read from statements: the\
  \ DIRECTION finding. chartLocus is a\npredicate on the IMAGE under picEtMap along\
  \ Over.testPoint (covariant, free); IsPlusHonest demands\na PREIMAGE under relPicToPicEt\
  \ at Gamma(T.left, U) (contravariant, the gap). And the genuine\nnear-miss to cite\
  \ is NOT an absence at all -- it is PicEtAff.unit_surjective_of_section\n(EffectivityClose.lean:141)\
  \ with .unitEquiv_of_section (:186), already recorded above.\n\n*** SHARPENED 2026-07-29\
  \ (review-ajcr, run 0082 s0006), answering ajcr-p2's question on I-0926.\nTHE OBSTRUCTION\
  \ IS A DIRECTION, NOT A BASE SHAPE -- so even my corrected \"base-shape\" wording\n\
  below is not the most useful framing. Use this one. ***\n\np2 asked whether the\
  \ coverage datum can be reduced to field points, since chartLocus is pointwise\n\
  via Over.testPoint: if so, base shape would not bind. MEASURED, from the two statements:\n\
  \n * chartLocus C m Z lam = {t | IsSplitWitness C (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t)\
  \ (chartTwist ..))}\n   (Pic0ChartLocus.lean:244-247). Membership is a predicate\
  \ on the IMAGE of lam under picEtMap.\n   Pushing forward is functorial, so the\
  \ passage to kappa(t) is FREE. LSP-checked the elaborated\n   type at :247: picEt\
  \ C (overSpec k (Over.testPointField t)).\n * IsPlusHonest C T mu = forall U : T.left.affineOpens,\
  \ EXISTS z, relPicToPicEt .. z = ..\n   (Pic0ChartPlusFibreProducer.lean:200-203).\
  \ This asks for a PREIMAGE at the ring Gamma(T.left, U).\n\nSo the free passage\
  \ is COVARIANT and the open obligation is CONTRAVARIANT. Knowing the fibre class\n\
  lies in relPic's image over the FIELD gives nothing at A: you would need the image\
  \ to descend along\nrelPic(A) -> relPic(kappa(t)), which is a spreading-out. MEASURED\
  \ that no such thing exists:\nIsPlusHonest has exactly SIX declarations tree-wide\
  \ (:200 def, .mul :209, .inv :220, .pow :230,\nchartLocusOpensOfIsPlusHonest :334,\
  \ mem_ :343) -- none a spreading-out, a field-point reduction or a\nlocalisation\
  \ statement. Zero LSP diagnostics on that file, so the absence is measured, not\
  \ grepped.\n\nCONSEQUENCE FOR A LANE ON THIS ROW. Do NOT spend a round on \"general\
  \ affine base -> field point\";\nthe missing direction is the descent. What IS a\
  \ real, self-contained brick, and is genuinely absent\nby the census above: a spreading-out\
  \ lemma for the RANGE of relPicToPicEt along a localisation\nA -> A_f. That is the\
  \ descent in miniature -- not cheap, but bounded and honestly stated.\n\nNOT WEAKENED\
  \ BY THIS: p2's landed Pic0ChartCoverageAffineTest.lean (chartsCoverLocally_of_affineLocal,\n\
  with converse) is a SITE fact and stands on its own; it buys a quantifier, as p2\
  \ said themselves.\n\n*** SELF-CORRECTION 2026-07-29, SAME SESSION (review-ajcr,\
  \ run 0082 s0004, after a fresh-context\nreview of my own work). THE IsPlusHonest\
  \ FINDING BELOW IS OVERSTATED ON THE STEP THAT CARRIES IT.\nThe route-decision conclusion\
  \ SURVIVES, for a different and better-evidenced reason. ***\n\nWHAT I GOT WRONG.\
  \ I argued: relPicToPicEt lands in PicEtAff.unit, unit is mk at the TRIVIAL cover\n\
  `.self A` alone, therefore honesty asserts that no nontrivial etale cover is needed.\
  \ That step is\nFALSE. PicEtAff.unit_eq_mk (Picard/RelPicCoverInjective.lean:48)\
  \ proves a unit class is presented on\nEVERY cover E, not only on `.self` -- so\
  \ \"mk at the trivial cover\" describes one PRESENTATION, not\nthe RANGE, and nothing\
  \ follows about which classes the range contains.\n\nAND THE ABSOLUTE FORM IS REFUTED\
  \ BY A LANDED THEOREM IN THIS TREE:\nPicEtAff.unit_surjective_of_section (Picard/EffectivityClose.lean:141)\
  \ proves the unit SURJECTIVE\nover a field test K admitting a curve point sigma,\
  \ upgraded to a MulEquiv by\nPicEtAff.unitEquiv_of_section (:186). Over such tests\
  \ honesty is DISCHARGED OUTRIGHT -- vacuously\ntrue, no etale cover needed anywhere.\
  \ So \"IsPlusHonest is the sheafification gap asserted of an\narbitrary section\"\
  \ is wrong as an absolute.\n\nTHE CORRECTED CLAIM, which is narrower and better\
  \ supported. The gap is at a GENERAL AFFINE BASE\nWITH NO SECTION, and the tree\
  \ documents exactly why:\n * the field route closes only through etale-cover cofinality\
  \ in finite separable field extensions\n   (Algebra.EtaleCover.exists_finiteSeparableField_algHom,\
  \ EtaleCover.lean:287) -- there is NO\n   general-base analogue of that cofinality;\n\
  \ * EffectivityMoving.lean:41-48 states plainly that for a merely quasi-finite (non-finite)\
  \ etale\n   cover the moving statement is FALSE, with a counterexample sketch (B\
  \ = A_u x A_v over a\n   2-dimensional normal local A with nontrivial local class\
  \ group). So the [Module.Finite A B]\n   hypothesis in the effectivity layer is\
  \ load-bearing, not convenience.\n\nSO THE OBSTRUCTION IS BASE-SHAPE, NOT ARBITRARINESS\
  \ OF THE CLASS. Two consequences:\n 1. the split to hand a prover lane is NOT \"\
  chart value (cheap) vs arbitrary section (blocked)\" but\n    \"field test with\
  \ a section (FREE) vs general sectionless affine base (OPEN)\". The delta between\n\
  \    the chart side and the coverage side is NARROWER than I priced it;\n 2. antecedent\
  \ 2 still owes a route decision -- which site coverage is local for -- because the\n\
  \    repair still refines covers and descends, and Zariski-local surjectivity still\
  \ will not absorb\n    that. The conclusion stands; cite the module-finiteness counterexample,\
  \ NOT the trivial-cover\n    claim, when repeating it.\n\nAlso corrected, same review:\
  \ I called DivisorFamilyAffThetaTyping.lean UNROOTED. It is ROOTED --\nAlgebraicJacobian.lean:346\
  \ imports it at HEAD (commit 2b8cef366) and its .olean exists, so it IS\nkernel-checked.\

  publishing. I-0941's step (i) is therefore already done; its step (ii) stands.\n\
  \n--- the original finding follows; read its trivial-cover reasoning as retracted\
  \ ---\n\n*** SECOND RE-PRICING 2026-07-29 (run 0082, review-ajcr, issue I-0920):\
  \ THE \"GENUINELY OPEN\nQUESTION\" BELOW IS NOT OPEN, IT IS THE ETALE-SHEAFIFICATION\
  \ GAP. Read this before targeting it. ***\n\nThe re-pricing further down is CORRECT\
  \ and stands: the producer exists\n(exists_isChartDatumPlusFibre_of_mem_range, Pic0ChartPlusFibreProducer.lean:178),\
  \ clause (i) is\npaid as DATA (chartLocusOpensOfIsPlusHonest, :334), and the residue\
  \ is the single hypothesis\nIsPlusHonest (:200). What was wrong is the NEXT sentence\
  \ -- \"THE GENUINELY OPEN QUESTION ... does\nIsPlusHonest hold for the class a COVERAGE\
  \ witness produces? A lane picking this row up should\ntarget that.\" A lane that\
  \ targets that will not find a proof, and here is why, read off the\nstatement rather\
  \ than the prose:\n\nIsPlusHonest C T mu says: for every affine open U of T.left,\
  \ mu|U is in the RANGE of\nrelPicToPicEt over Gamma(T.left,U) -- i.e. Zariski-locally\
  \ the class comes from the UN-sheafified\nrelPic. But picEt is built on PicEtAff\
  \ (PicEt.lean:9-21), and PicEtAff C A (PicEtAff.lean:218) is a\nQUOTIENT OVER ALL\
  \ ETALE COVERS, whose elements are PicEtAff.mk E x; PicEtAff.unit (:377) -- the\n\
  target of relPicToPicEt (PicEtUnit.lean:126) -- is mk at the TRIVIAL cover `.self\
  \ A` ALONE. So\nhonesty asserts that no nontrivial etale cover is needed on that\
  \ piece, which is precisely what the\none-step plus construction exists to allow\
  \ to FAIL.\n\nThe project already says this at the one place it measured it. Pic0ChartHonest.lean's\
  \ own \"What this\ndoes and does not give\": honesty is obtained \"OVER Spec E.Carrier,\
  \ NOT over Spec A\" -- purchased by\nCHANGING THE BASE (a cover splits over its\
  \ own carrier), with \"Nothing here performs that descent\".\n\nWHICH CASES ARE\

  \ property (.mul/.inv/.pow/\nchartTwist_isPlusHonest). None concludes it for a class\
  \ given as an arbitrary element of picEt. The\nchart value IS abelDiv * Sigma *\
  \ (theta^m)^{-1}, so the discharged cases cover it -- that is exactly\nwhy this\
  \ row could be re-priced downward at all, and that part is real.\n\nWHERE IT BITES:\
  \ coverage, and only coverage. chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise\n(Pic0ChartCoveragePointwise.lean:128)\
  \ quantifies over EVERY s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T) and\nmust produce a\
  \ chart point hitting it. Arbitrariness is the whole content of coverage; restricting\n\
  s to chart-value shape makes the statement circular. So:\n * honesty of coverage's\
  \ own WITNESS -- cheap, fine, already covered;\n * honesty of the class s it must\

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyZarSheaf

/-!
# The divisor functor (DD-2 S6b)

The one-screen functor packaging of the locally certified divisor vehicle
(`informal/spec-dd-2.md` §6, spelling (A) of I-0222, co-signed by the DD-R lane):

* `AlgebraicGeometry.divFunctor`: `(Over (Spec k))ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u`, with object values
  `divFamZar C π n T` and action `divFamZar.map` — the `picEtFunctor` house pattern.
  Type-valued: degree-`n` divisor families carry no group structure.

This is the functor `divRep` is stated against (`informal/spec-dd-r.md` §3 item 8,
Addendum 1).  The sheaf halves are consumed as-is from
`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyZarSheaf` (`ext_of_le_cover` /
`existsUnique_glue_of_le_cover`), the pic0/01JJ precedent.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
/- `lake env lean` drops the lakefile's `[leanOptions]` (I-0161), so the pinned synthesis
depth must be set in-file for the faithful per-file check. -/
set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

universe u

open CategoryTheory

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

attribute [local instance] Over.sectionsAlgebra Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
variable (π : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsAffineHom π] (n : ℕ)

/-- **The divisor functor** (DD-2 S6b, the pinned name): the locally certified
degree-`n` divisor families as a presheaf of types on the slice over `Spec k`,
with the glued restriction `divFamZar.map` along arbitrary test morphisms — the
`picDegLayerFunctor` house pattern. -/
noncomputable def divFunctor : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u where
  obj T := divFamZar C π n T.unop
  map g := ↾divFamZar.map C π n g.unop
  map_id T := by
    ext s U
    exact congrArg (fun z : divFamZar C π n T.unop => z.1 U) (divFamZar.map_id C π n s)
  map_comp {T T' T''} g h := by
    ext s U
    exact congrArg (fun z : divFamZar C π n T''.unop => z.1 U)
      (divFamZar.map_comp C π n g.unop h.unop s)

@[simp]
lemma divFunctor_obj (T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ) :
    (divFunctor C π n).obj T = divFamZar C π n T.unop :=
  rfl

@[simp]
lemma divFunctor_map {T T' : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ} (g : T ⟶ T')
    (s : divFamZar C π n T.unop) :
    (divFunctor C π n).map g s = divFamZar.map C π n g.unop s :=
  rfl

end AlgebraicGeometry

8	/-!
9	# `RestrictedChartFibre` is inhabited, and where the content of antecedent 1 actually sits
10	
11	`Picard/Pic0ChartRestrictedFibre.lean` repairs the route to `IsChartUniv` — antecedent 1 of
12	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` — by demanding the fibre datum at the **restricted** chart.  Its
13	own "honest limits" section then recorded the thing it could not settle:
14	
15	> an inhabitant at `V = ⊥` was **attempted and not obtained** in this session … the `sq` field
16	> … needs `Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C (Over.mk a₁))` over an empty base.  That is the
17	> triviality of `picEt` over the empty scheme: true, a genuinely separate lemma, and absent
18	> from the tree.
19	
20	**That pricing was wrong, and the error was in the reduction rather than in the census.**  The
21	`sq` goal is an equality of two elements of `(pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op S)` at an *empty* test
22	`S`, and `pic0SigmaSheaf` is a **sheaf**.  A sheaf's value at an object covered by the empty
23	sieve is terminal, so the goal is closed with no fact about `picEt` at all:
24	
25	* `Scheme.bot_mem_grothendieckTopology` (mathlib, `Sites/Pretopology.lean`) — stated exactly for
26	  `[IsEmpty X]`;
27	* `Sheaf.isTerminalOfBotCover` (mathlib, `Sites/Sheaf.lean`).
28	
29	The `congr 1` that peeled the Σ-component and named `pic0Subgroup` as the residue is what made
30	a free goal look like a missing lemma.  Recorded because the prose pricing outlived the check.
31	
32	## What this file establishes
33	
34	* `pic0Sigma_obj_subsingleton_of_isEmpty` — the sheaf value at an empty test is a subsingleton.
35	  Three lines, no `picEt` input, no geometry.
36	* `restrictedChartFibre_bot` — **`RestrictedChartFibre` at `V = ⊥` is inhabited,
37	  unconditionally**: for every `rep`, `m`, `Z`, `hdeg`.  So the class is non-empty and the
38	  unmeasured-inhabitation risk `Pic0ChartRestrictedFibre.lean` flagged against itself (and that
39	  `ChartTyping` and `IsChartLocusFibre` carried) is discharged for this class.
40	* `isChartUniv_bot` — hence `IsChartUniv C π n rep m Z hdeg ⊥` holds with **no hypothesis**.
41	* `isOpenImmersion_presheaf_restrictChart_bot` — the same construction for an **arbitrary** chart
42	  map, which is what the `⊥` witness really rests on: a lane that gets `hf` at `⊥` has learned
43	  nothing about its own chart.
44	* `range_subset_range_top_ι`,
45	  `isOpenImmersion_presheaf_abelSigmaChart_of_restrictedChartFibre_top` and
46	  `not_restrictedChartFibre_top_of_not_injective` — the opposite end of the interval.
47	* `restrictedChartFibre_top_iff` — at `V = ⊤` the class is **equivalent** to
48	  `IsChartLocusFibre`, which retires the latter as an independent obligation and supplies the
49	  converse `Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean:55` claims exists under a name nothing defines.
50	
51	## The consequence, and it is a statement about the seam rather than about this file
52	
53	`isChartUniv_bot` says antecedent 1 **carries no content at `V = ⊥`**.  That is not a defect of
54	the repair, and it is *not* a vacuity of the coupled assembly — because the coverage side is
55	refuted at the same value:
56	
57	* `not_coverageContainment_bot` — the `hcov` hypothesis of
58	  `pic0RepresentableBy_of_restrictedChartFibre_of_coverage` at `V = ⊥` is **false** as soon as
59	  some test has a point.  Its witness `x` would have range inside `Set.range ((⊥).ι.base) = ∅`
60	  while `t ∈ W` exhibits a point of the source.
61	
62	## Both ends of the `V`-interval, and why the coupling has an interior
63	
64	The two endpoints are priced in **opposite** directions, and that is the file's main content:
65	
66	* at `V = ⊥`: `hf` is **free** (`restrictedChartFibre_bot`), and coverage's containment is
67	  **impossible** (`not_coverageContainment_bot`);
68	* at `V = ⊤`: coverage's containment is **free** (`range_subset_range_top_ι`), and `hf` is the
69	  **unrestricted certificate** (`isOpenImmersion_presheaf_abelSigmaChart_of_…_top`).
70	
71	At `⊤` the restricted datum returns exactly the certificate the restriction was introduced to
72	avoid — the one `Pic0AtlasFromDivRep.lean:54`, `Pic0ChartPair.lean:14` and
73	`Pic0ChartOpenImmersionCriterion.lean:214` assert to be false for the Abel chart.  So the
74	restriction is not a formality that a lane could undo by taking `V` large.
75	
76	Hence **no endpoint discharges the assembly**, and any `V` that works must be a proper
77	intermediate open (`not_restrictedChartFibre_top_of_not_injective` makes the `⊤` end an outright
78	refutation, conditional on the `abel-noninj` fork).  That is what the chart locus is for, and it
79	is why CHART-U(b)'s openness is a real obligation rather than bookkeeping: neither an `hf` lane
80	nor a coverage lane can retreat to a convenient `V`.
81	
82	**What this is NOT, and an earlier draft of this header claimed otherwise** (`I-1012`, filed by a
83	fresh-context review of this file).  The two endpoints are **not** a non-vacuity check for the
84	coupled assembly.  Non-vacuity of a pair `(huniv V, hcov V)` needs a `V` where both hold — or a
85	refutation at every `V` — and two *bad* values of `V` supply neither.  The pair still has **no
86	measured inhabitant at any `V`**, and nothing here excludes it being unsatisfiable everywhere.
87	What *is* discharged is inhabitation of `RestrictedChartFibre` alone, at `⊥`, which is strictly
88	weaker.  The sentence above ("any `V` that works must be a proper intermediate open") is a
89	conditional and must not be read as an existence claim.  So `necessity_of_restrictedChartFibre`
90	was not the assembly's non-vacuity check (`I-0937`), and neither is this file; the assembly's
91	non-vacuity is **open**.
92	
93	A further limit the endpoints do not reach: at `V = ⊥` the *instance* form
94	`pic0RepresentableBy_of_restrictedChartFibre` goes through with `huniv` supplied free by
95	`restrictedChartFibre_bot`, leaving the `IsLocallySurjective` instance binder as the sole
96	remaining antecedent.  `not_coverageContainment_bot` constrains the `hcov` *spelling* of coverage,
97	not that instance binder — so it does not by itself rule out a `⊥`-based route through the
98	instance version.
99	
100	**What is still NOT closed, stated plainly.**  `rep` remains a hypothesis with no producer, so
101	`IsChartUniv` is not even statable without it; `hcov` at a useful `V` has no producer; and
102	nothing here produces a chart at a `V` other than `⊥`.  No antecedent of
103	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` is discharged by this file.  What is discharged is the
104	*satisfiability question* about the class, plus the sharp localisation of the remaining
105	obligation.
106	-/

124	/-! ## The empty test, from the sheaf axiom -/
125	
126	/-- **The Σ-sheaf is trivial on an empty test** — by the sheaf axiom, not by any property of
127	`picEt`.
128	
129	The empty sieve covers an empty scheme (`Scheme.bot_mem_grothendieckTopology`), and a sheaf's
130	value at an object with a `⊥` cover is terminal (`Sheaf.isTerminalOfBotCover`); a terminal
131	object of `Type u` is a subsingleton.

133	This is the declaration `Pic0ChartRestrictedFibre.lean` priced as "the triviality of `picEt`
134	over the empty scheme: true, a genuinely separate lemma, and absent from the tree".  Note what
135	does *not* appear: no `picEt`, no `pic0Subgroup`, no `relPic`, no curve geometry.  The residue

138	    Subsingleton ((pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op S)) :=

174	  refine ⟨⟨⊥, isInitialOfIsEmpty.to _, ?_, ?_⟩⟩
175	  · ext S x
176	    have : IsEmpty (S.unop : Scheme.{u}) := x.base.hom.1.isEmpty
177	    exact (pic0Sigma_obj_subsingleton_of_isEmpty (C := C) S.unop).elim _ _

10	
11	`Picard/Pic0ChartPair.lean` pins `IsChartUniv` — the `hf` half of the `(f, hf)` pair that
12	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes — and its docstring, together with the `c9b` roadmap

17	`MorphismProperty.relative` at `yoneda` (mathlib `MorphismProperty/Representable.lean`), and
18	`relative` is *by definition* a conjunction of two independent statements:
19	
20	1. **relative representability** — for every test `T` and every `g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ 𝓟`, the
21	   fibre product of the chart map along `g` is representable *by a scheme*;
22	2. **the property clause** — every represented pullback is an open immersion of schemes.
23	
24	The GAP-2/classifier story is the input to (2) only: it is what makes the fibre a single
25	point, hence the represented pullback an open subscheme.  It says nothing about (1), which
26	is a representability statement about a fibre product.  Read as one clause, a lane waits on
27	CERT-Σ for both halves.  Read as two, half of the work is stateable and provable *now*, with
28	no divisor-representability endpoint and no certificate anywhere in it.

32	Everything here is stated for an **arbitrary** morphism of big-site presheaves
33	`f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1` and an **arbitrary** open `V ⊆ X`.  No `divRep`
34	endpoint, no certificate, no `Z`, no `θ` and no chart index appears in any statement.  That

36	the divisor-representability shape enters only at the instantiation.
37	
38	The criterion's hypotheses are **elementwise** conditions on the presheaf — a fibrewise
39	injectivity clause and a clause producing the representing open — because that is what
40	mathlib's `MorphismProperty.relative.of_exists` reduces the goal to once the presheaf
41	category's pullbacks are computed pointwise (`Types.isPullback_iff`).

45	* `AlgebraicGeometry.ChartFibrePresented` — the elementwise datum (1) needs: for each test
46	  point `g` of the target, an open `W` of the test and an identification of the `W`-points

120	  chart value.  For the Abel chart this is `chartLocus`;
121	* `r` recovers the chart point: over `W`, the divisor family whose class `g` is;
122	* `sq` says the two ways round agree;
123	* `exists_factor` is the honest content — a test point of `X` and a test point of `T` with
124	  the *same* class come from a unique point of `W`.  Existence is coverage-on-the-locus;
125	  the uniqueness half is *not* a field here, because it is free: `W.ι` is a monomorphism.
126	
127	Nothing in this structure mentions a divisor scheme, a certificate, a twist or a chart
128	index.  It is a statement about a morphism of presheaves and an open of a test. -/
129	structure ChartFibrePresented {X T : Scheme.{u}}
130	    (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) (g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
131	    where
132	  /-- The locus of the test where the class named by `g` is a chart value. -/
133	  W : T.Opens
134	  /-- The chart point over that locus. -/
135	  r : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X
136	  /-- The square commutes: `r` names the class `g` restricted to `W`. -/
137	  sq : yoneda.map r ≫ f = yoneda.map W.ι ≫ g
138	  /-- **Coverage on the locus**: an `S`-point of `X` and an `S`-point of `T` carrying the
139	  same class factor through `W`, compatibly with both projections. -/
140	  exists_factor : ∀ (S : Scheme.{u}) (v : S ⟶ X) (w : S ⟶ T),
141	    f.app (op S) v = g.app (op S) w → ∃ u : S ⟶ (W : Scheme.{u}), u ≫ r = v ∧ u ≫ W.ι = w
142	
143	namespace ChartFibrePresented
144	
145	variable {X T : Scheme.{u}} {f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1}
146	  {g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1}
147	
148	/-- **The datum presents the fibre product**: the square of `ChartFibrePresented` is a
149	pullback of presheaves.
150	
151	Pullbacks in a presheaf category are computed pointwise
152	(`IsPullback.of_forall_isPullback_app`), and a pointwise pullback of types is exactly
153	"commutes + jointly injective + jointly surjective" (`Types.isPullback_iff`).  The first is
154	`sq`, the third is `exists_factor`, and the second is free from `W.ι` being a
155	monomorphism — which is where the openness of `W` does its work. -/
156	theorem isPullback (D : ChartFibrePresented C f g) :
157	    IsPullback (yoneda.map D.r) (yoneda.map D.W.ι) f g := by
158	  refine IsPullback.of_forall_isPullback_app fun S => ?_
159	  rw [Types.isPullback_iff]
160	  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
161	  · exact congrArg (fun φ : yoneda.obj (D.W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1 =>
162	      φ.app S) D.sq
163	  · -- joint injectivity: already forced by `W.ι` alone, being a monomorphism
164	    rintro u₁ u₂ ⟨-, h₂⟩
165	    have : u₁ ≫ D.W.ι = u₂ ≫ D.W.ι := h₂
166	    exact (cancel_mono D.W.ι).mp this
167	  · -- joint surjectivity: `exists_factor` at the test `S.unop`
168	    intro v w hvw
169	    obtain ⟨u, hu₁, hu₂⟩ := D.exists_factor S.unop v w hvw
170	    exact ⟨u, hu₁, hu₂⟩
171	
172	end ChartFibrePresented
173	
174	/-- **THE CRITERION** — `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` from elementwise data, discharging BOTH
175	clauses of `MorphismProperty.relative` at once.
176	
177	Given, for every test point of the target sheaf, a `ChartFibrePresented` datum, the chart map
178	is an open immersion of presheaves.  Certificate-free, divRep-free, and with no reference to
179	divisors: the input is a family of opens of tests together with the coverage statement on
180	each.
181	
182	This is the honest shape of `IsChartUniv`'s obligation.  Reading `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf`
183	as a single "relative GAP-2" statement conflates:
184	
185	* **relative representability** — that the fibre product is a scheme at all.  Supplied here
186	  by `W`, an open subscheme of the test, and proved by `ChartFibrePresented.isPullback`;
187	* **the property clause** — that each represented pullback is an open immersion.  Supplied
188	  here by `W.ι` being an open immersion, which is free.
189	
190	What is *not* free, and is the whole mathematical content, is `exists_factor`: a class that
191	agrees with a chart value must come from the locus.  For the Abel chart that is the relative
192	form of DAT-C GAP-2 (uniqueness of the normalized effective representative) fed through the
193	classifier — so the CERT-Σ gate is real, but it gates ONE field of ONE structure rather than
194	the whole certificate. -/
195	theorem isOpenImmersion_presheaf_of_chartFibrePresented {X : Scheme.{u}}
196	    (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
197	    (D : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1),
198	      ChartFibrePresented C f g) :
199	    IsOpenImmersion.presheaf f := by
200	  refine MorphismProperty.relative.of_exists fun T g => ?_
201	  exact ⟨(D T g).W, yoneda.map (D T g).r, (D T g).W.ι, (D T g).isPullback,
202	    inferInstance⟩
203	
204	/-! ## The criterion is not vacuous
205	
206	A structure whose hard field is an existential can be inhabited for trivial reasons, and a
207	criterion built on one is then worthless.  This section rules that out **by proof** rather
208	than by inspection: the datum is unconstructible exactly when it must be. -/
209	
210	/-- **Non-vacuity of `ChartFibrePresented`, from the necessary direction.**
211	
212	If a chart map fails to be injective on the points of even one test, then no family of
213	`ChartFibrePresented` data exists for it.  In particular the criterion cannot be satisfied
214	for the *unrestricted* Abel chart, whose non-injectivity is the linear system `|D|`
215	(`Pic0AtlasFromDivRep.lean:54`): the criterion's hypothesis is genuinely as strong as the
216	conclusion, and `exists_factor` is not a clause one can talk one's way past.
217	
218	The proof composes the two halves of this file, which is the point of having both. -/
219	theorem isEmpty_forall_chartFibrePresented_of_not_injective {X : Scheme.{u}}
220	    (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) (T : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ)
221	    (hT : ¬ Function.Injective (f.app T)) :
222	    IsEmpty (∀ (T' : Scheme.{u}) (g : yoneda.obj T' ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1),
223	        ChartFibrePresented C f g) :=
224	  ⟨fun D => hT (injective_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf
225	    (isOpenImmersion_presheaf_of_chartFibrePresented f D) T)⟩
226	
227	/-- The same statement in the form a lane will meet it: the criterion's input **implies**
228	elementwise injectivity on every test.  So a lane that cannot prove uniqueness of the
229	normalized effective representative cannot supply the datum either — the CERT-Σ gate is not
230	an artefact of how `IsChartUniv` was pinned. -/
231	theorem injective_of_chartFibrePresented {X : Scheme.{u}}
232	    (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
233	    (D : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1),
234	      ChartFibrePresented C f g) (T : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ) :
235	    Function.Injective (f.app T) :=
236	  injective_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf
237	    (isOpenImmersion_presheaf_of_chartFibrePresented f D) T
238	
239	end
240	
241	end AlgebraicGeometry

9	/-!
10	# The coupling of the atlas open to the coverage witness
11	
12	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` (`Picard/Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:161`) has three antecedents, and
13	the board tracks them on three separate rows: `IsChartUniv` (c9b), Zariski-local surjectivity
14	of `Sigma.desc f` (dat-b B-6), and `rep i` (divrep).  Reading those rows one concludes the
15	three compose — discharge each and the seam fires.
16	
17	**They do not compose as stated.**  The atlas the seam consumes is a family of *restricted*
18	charts `restrictChart (abelSigmaChart …) (V i)` (`Picard/Pic0ChartAtlasParamFree.lean:86`),
19	whose source is `(V i : Scheme)` — an open of the *chart source*, i.e. of the divisor scheme.
20	So the coverage antecedent, unfolded through `chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise`
21	(`Pic0ChartCoveragePointwise.lean:128`), must produce a chart point
22	`x : (W : Scheme) ⟶ (V i : Scheme)` landing **in that same `V i`**, while coverage geometry
23	produces a point of the divisor scheme `D.left` with no such constraint.  The two opens the
24	route wants to identify live on different objects — `V i` on the divisor scheme, `chartLocus`
25	on the test — and no declaration in the tree relates them.
26	
27	That is an obligation *between* two antecedents, owned by no row, and it is why "close c9b,
28	then close B-6" would not have composed even with both closed.
29	
30	## What this file does about it
31	
32	It names the coupling and derives restricted coverage from unrestricted coverage together
33	with a range containment: the coverage witness, viewed in the chart source, factors
34	set-theoretically through `V i`.  Given that, the witness lifts to `V i` along the open
35	immersion `(V i).ι` by `IsOpenImmersion.lift`, and the class it names is unchanged because
36	`restrictChart` is *by definition* precomposition with `yoneda.map (V i).ι` — so the lift's
37	chart value is the unlifted one, with no transport.
38	
39	**THREE CORRECTIONS TO AN EARLIER DRAFT OF THIS HEADER**, all from a fresh-context audit
40	(2026-07-29, inbox `I-0894`), because each would have mispriced the row:
41	
42	1. the hypothesis is **NOT "weaker than either antecedent"**, as the draft claimed.  It is the
43	   unrestricted coverage datum **conjoined** with the containment, so it *implies* the
44	   coverage antecedent and is strictly STRONGER than it.  What is true is the much smaller
45	   claim that the containment is all that separates unrestricted from restricted coverage;
46	2. `liftPointwiseToOpens` and `pointwise_of_pointwise_restrictChart` together are one
47	   **biconditional**, and its transport step (`restrictChart_app_apply`) is `rfl`.  So this
48	   file is a *repackaging with its difference named*, and **it closes no gate**.  It is
49	   reported as routing information, not as progress on any antecedent;
50	3. the draft argued about "`V i = chartLocus`" in two places.  **Those carriers do not meet**:
51	   `V i : (X i).Opens` is an open of the chart source (the divisor scheme), while
52	   `chartLocus C m Z lam : Set ↥T.left` is a set on a *test*.  The only bridge is
53	   `chartLocusOpens`, which lands in `T.left.Opens` and costs `haff` (= dat-b's B-4).  The
54	   mismatch is precisely what this file was written to expose, so reasoning as though the two
55	   were interchangeable — as the draft did below — defeated the purpose.
56	
57	What survives all three: the containment is genuine content (probes below), it is exactly the
58	difference between the two coverage statements (the converse), and no declaration in the tree
59	relates the two carriers.
60	
61	## Main declarations
62	
63	* `AlgebraicGeometry.PointwiseCoverage` — the pointwise coverage datum of B-5, named for an
64	  arbitrary chart family so the two atlases (unrestricted, restricted) can be compared.
65	* `AlgebraicGeometry.liftPointwiseToOpens` — **the coupling**: pointwise coverage for a family
66	  `f` plus the range containment gives pointwise coverage for the *restricted* family
67	  `fun i => restrictChart (f i) (V i)`.
68	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallySurjective_restrictChart_of_pointwise` — the composite into the
69	  instance the seam consumes, for the restricted atlas.
70	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pointwise_of_pointwise_restrictChart` — the **converse**: restricted
71	  coverage gives unrestricted coverage *and* the containment.  So `hV` is not a hypothesis
72	  chosen for provability — it is exactly the difference between the two, and a lane cannot
73	  reach the restricted atlas while avoiding it.

77	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

79	universe u
80	
81	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
82	
83	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
84	
85	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
86	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
87	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
88	
89	noncomputable section
90	
91	variable (C) in
92	/-- **The pointwise coverage datum of B-5**, named.
93	
94	This is verbatim the hypothesis of `chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise`
95	(`Pic0ChartCoveragePointwise.lean:128`), given a name so that the same statement can be
96	compared at two different chart families — which is the whole point of this file: B-6 is
97	consumed at the *restricted* atlas, while coverage geometry produces the datum at the
98	*unrestricted* one. -/
99	def PointwiseCoverage {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
100	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) : Prop :=
101	  ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : ↥T),
102	    ∃ (W : T.Opens) (_ : t ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
103	      (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s
104	
105	/-! ## The chart value of a restricted chart at a lifted point -/
106	
107	/-- **A restricted chart reads a lifted point exactly as the unrestricted chart reads the
108	point itself.**
109	
110	`restrictChart f V` is `yoneda.map V.ι ≫ f` by definition, so its value at `u` is the value
111	of `f` at `u ≫ V.ι`.  No transport, no naturality of `f` — the composition is on the source
112	side, where `yoneda.map` is precomposition.
113	
114	This is the entire reason the coupling below is cheap, and it is worth isolating: a lane that
115	expected the two chart values to differ by a restriction map would look for a compatibility

117	lemma restrictChart_app_apply {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
118	    (V : X.Opens) {S : Scheme.{u}} (u : S ⟶ (V : Scheme.{u})) :
119	    (restrictChart f V).app (op S) u = f.app (op S) (u ≫ V.ι) :=
120	  rfl

140	deliberately does not assume an answer — in particular `V i` is an open of the chart source

142	instantiation still owes the `chartLocusOpens` bridge (cost: `haff`, i.e. dat-b's B-4). -/
143	theorem liftPointwiseToOpens {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
144	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) (V : ∀ i, (X i).Opens)

147	        (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s ∧
148	          Set.range (x.base) ⊆ Set.range ((V i).ι.base)) :

150	  intro T s t
151	  obtain ⟨W, htW, i, x, hx, hrange⟩ := h T s t
152	  refine ⟨W, htW, i, IsOpenImmersion.lift ((V i).ι) x hrange, ?_⟩
153	  rw [restrictChart_app_apply, IsOpenImmersion.lift_fac]
154	  exact hx

158	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes *at the restricted atlas* — which is the atlas
159	`mixedParamRepresentableBy` (`Pic0ChartAtlasParamFree.lean:125`) and every real chart family
160	is built from.
161	
162	Stated because this, not `isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_pointwise`, is what a coverage lane
163	owes when the atlas is restricted: the two differ by exactly `hV`. -/
164	theorem isLocallySurjective_restrictChart_of_pointwise {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
165	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) (V : ∀ i, (X i).Opens)
166	    (h : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : ↥T),
167	      ∃ (W : T.Opens) (_ : t ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
168	        (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s ∧
169	          Set.range (x.base) ⊆ Set.range ((V i).ι.base)) :
170	    Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology
171	      (Sigma.desc (fun i => restrictChart (f i) (V i))) :=
172	  isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_pointwise C _ (liftPointwiseToOpens C f V h)
173	
174	/-! ## The converse: `hV` is the exact difference, not a convenient extra
175	
176	A coupling lemma whose hypothesis is stronger than the gap it bridges hides the gap instead of
177	naming it.  This section rules that out: restricted coverage gives back unrestricted coverage
178	together with the containment, so `hV` is precisely what separates the two. -/
179	
180	variable (C) in
181	/-- **The converse of the coupling.**  Pointwise coverage for the restricted family gives
182	pointwise coverage for `f` *and* the range containment at the produced witness.
183

190	and whose chart value under `f i` is the restricted chart's value at `x` by

192	theorem pointwise_of_pointwise_restrictChart {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
193	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) (V : ∀ i, (X i).Opens)
194	    (h : PointwiseCoverage C (fun i => restrictChart (f i) (V i))) :
195	    ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : ↥T),
196	      ∃ (W : T.Opens) (_ : t ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
197	        (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s ∧
198	          Set.range (x.base) ⊆ Set.range ((V i).ι.base) := by
199	  intro T s t
200	  obtain ⟨W, htW, i, u, hu⟩ := h T s t
201	  refine ⟨W, htW, i, u ≫ (V i).ι, hu, ?_⟩
202	  intro z hz
203	  obtain ⟨w, rfl⟩ := hz
204	  exact ⟨u.base w, rfl⟩
205	
206	end

/-! ## The locally certified divisor-functor value -/

variable (C R π)
variable (n : ℕ)

/-- The divisor-equality setoid on locally certified systems (Addendum 2's mirror of
`divFamSetoid`): the underlying local-equation systems cut the same divisor; the local
certificates are per-representative data and do not enter the relation. -/
def divFamZarSetoid : Setoid {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations //
    IsLocallyCertified C R π n d} where
  r d₁ d₂ := Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq d₁.1 d₂.1
  iseqv :=
    ⟨fun d => Scheme.LocalEquations.divEq_refl d.1,
     fun h => h.symm, fun h h' => h.trans h'⟩

/-- **The locally certified divisor-functor value on the affine test `R`**
(`informal/spec-dd-2.md`, Addendum 2): locally certified local-equation systems of
degree `n` up to divisor equality. This is the carrier on which the divisor functor is
a Zariski sheaf — the globally certified `DivFam` remains the building block. -/
def DivFamZar : Type u := Quotient (divFamZarSetoid C R π n)

namespace DivFamZar

variable {C R π n}

/-- The class of a locally certified system. -/
def mk (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations) (hd : IsLocallyCertified C R π n d) :
    DivFamZar C R π n :=
  Quotient.mk (divFamZarSetoid C R π n) ⟨d, hd⟩

lemma mk_eq_mk_iff {d₁ d₂ : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
    {h₁ : IsLocallyCertified C R π n d₁} {h₂ : IsLocallyCertified C R π n d₂} :
    mk d₁ h₁ = mk d₂ h₂ ↔ Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq d₁ d₂ :=
  Quotient.eq (r := divFamZarSetoid C R π n)

/-- **The Picard class of a locally certified divisor class** `𝒪(D)`: well defined on
the quotient by `picClass_eq_of_divEq`. -/
noncomputable def picClass (F : DivFamZar C R π n) : (relCurve C R).CechPic :=
  Quotient.lift
    (fun d : {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations // IsLocallyCertified C R π n d} =>
      d.1.picClass)
    (fun _ _ h => Scheme.LocalEquations.picClass_eq_of_divEq h) F

@[simp]
lemma picClass_mk (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations)
    (hd : IsLocallyCertified C R π n d) : picClass (mk d hd) = d.picClass :=
  rfl

end DivFamZar

variable {C R π n}

/-- **The comparison from the globally certified value**: a certified family is
locally certified (trivial cover), and divisor equality is the relation on both
sides. Over a field the two notions agree; over a general base `toZar` is the
sheafification-of-value comparison. -/
def DivFam.toZar : DivFam C R π n → DivFamZar C R π n :=
  Quotient.lift
    (fun F : CertifiedDivisorFamily C R π n =>
      DivFamZar.mk F.eqns F.isLocallyCertified)
    (fun _ _ h => DivFamZar.mk_eq_mk_iff.mpr h)

@[simp]
lemma DivFam.toZar_mk (F : CertifiedDivisorFamily C R π n) :
    (DivFam.mk F).toZar = DivFamZar.mk F.eqns F.isLocallyCertified :=
  rfl

variable (C) in
/-- **CHART-U(a), `chartLocus`** (`w4-datc` §3.3, co-signed `w4-datb` §1.6): the set of
points of a general test `T` at which the twisted fibre class `λ_t · θ^m · (−Σ)` has, after
some finite separable splitting of the collapsed plus class at `κ(t)`, an effective witness
divisor with vanishing `H¹`.

The three layers, each supplied by a named brick:
* the *point-to-field-point* passage is `Over.testPoint` (input 0 of this brick — the one
  nothing in the tree had);
* the *twist* is `chartTwist`, the class-side avatar of `chartValue`;
* the *split witness reading over a field* is `IsSplitWitness`.

This is the RESERVED name of `Pic0ChartLocusClass.lean`'s header, now defined.  Note it is
strictly stronger than `cechWitnessLocus`: general test, twisted class, split predicate. -/
def chartLocus (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (lam : picEt C T) : Set T.left :=
  {t : T.left | IsSplitWitness C
    (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) (chartTwist C m Z T lam))}

theorem mem_chartLocus_iff (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (lam : picEt C T) (t : T.left) :
    t ∈ chartLocus C m Z lam ↔ IsSplitWitness C
      (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) (chartTwist C m Z T lam)) :=
  Iff.rfl

The witness clause of `IsSplitWitness` is stated on a presenting Čech class over `C_L`.
